the polymorphic capabilities of Genetically Programmed Neural Networks can be used to evolve distributed programs, rule based systems and neural networks.

the study of the emergence of complex adaptive behaviour through the interaction of simple computational agents, and with the study of genetic algorithms as a mechanism for evolution of such systems.
the study of the polymorphic and hybridization abilities of Genetically Programmed networks and their applications to the development of complex adaptive systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Genetically Programmed networks are a powerful and promising tool for the development of distributed systems.
Genetically Programmed networks can be a good choice for solving problems where a distributed representation of the solution is more appropriate.

the polymorphic abilities and hybridization of Genetically Programmed networks allow the user to control the evolutionary process and the search space, which can result in the discovery of better solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new distributed representation, called Genetically-Programmed Network, for genetic programming, which can be easily evolved into a distributed system, a rule based expert system or a neural net, and which allows the exploration of different network topologies, thus increasing the possibility to find a (or a best) solution.
Genetically Programmed Nets can evolve solutions for problems that are difficult to solve with traditional genetic programming, and they can do so faster than other approaches.
we have developed a distributed representation that is capable of evolving a wide range of solutions, from neural networks to rule based systems, in an efficient manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

polymorphy can be achieved by a simple modification to the evolutionary algorithm and can be used to increase the search capabilities of a system, thus increasing the probability of finding a (better) solution.

the polymorphic abilities and the flexibility in the network topology of Genetically Programmed networks allow for an easy exploration of the search space, which in turn can lead to the discovery of solutions to complex problems.
the polymorphic abilities in GP can be extended to the network topology level.
